{{infobox biome | title = Swamp | image = Biome swamp.png | caption = | passive = * [[Giant Herring]] | hostile = * [[Blob]] * [[Oozer]] * [[Draugr]] * [[Draugr Elite]] * [[Leech]] * [[Skeleton]] * [[Surtling]] * [[Wraith]] * [[Writhan]] * [[Abomination]] | boss = [[Bonemass]] | unique = * [[Ancient Bark]] * [[Scrap Iron]] * [[Guck]] * [[Turnip Seeds]] | regular = | food = | structures = * [[Geyser]] * [[Abandoned Hut]] * [[Swamp Runestone Tower]] * [[Inverted Tower]] * [[Swamp Grave]] * [[Shipwreck]] | dungeons = [[Sunken Crypts]] | npcs = [[The Bog Witch]] }} The '''Swamp''' is an oppressive [[Biomes|biome]], filled with massive trees, muddy bogs, and hostile creatures. Immense, bare-branched [[Ancient Tree|Ancient Trees]] claw at a sickly cloud-laden sky, making for intimidating vistas. On what small bit of ground exists, tendrils of sodden soil snake around and through the knee-deep, plague-ridden water that permeates the entire biome. [[Draugr]] stumble about everywhere, watching and waiting to slay any living Viking they can find; to prove they are worthy of ascension to gods that have long since stopped listening. From a difficulty standpoint, the Swamps were designed to be a wall of sorts. Entering the biome for the first time, Vikings are met with an unprecedented drive by the very land to kill them as quickly and effectively as possible: every last creature here is hostile to the player. It is always raining in the mire regardless of the weather elsewhere; this means the player will always be [[Wet Effect|Wet]] when traversing the terrain. The toll taken on stamina in the Swamp is brutal, especially at night, when the player will also be [[Cold Effect|Cold]], and likely on the run from [[Wraith|Wraiths]]. The presence of [[Poison]] is undeniable as well, being the weapon of choice for [[Oozer]]s, [[Blob]]s, and [[Leech]]es. Making express use of a certain [[Poison Resistance Mead|mead]] unlocked in the previous biome is not negotiable. Sprinkling the landscape of any moderately large Swamp are [[Sunken Crypts]], which require a [[Swamp Key]] to unlock. These crypts sit in a state of near ruin, their winding corridors caved in and blocked by [[Muddy Scrap Pile]]s, which can be mined for [[Scrap Iron]], [[Leather Scraps]], and [[Withered Bone]]s. Up on the surface, half-submerged abandoned structures and [[Monster Spawner|hostile creature spawners]] can be found, as well as the occasional [[Geyser|Surtling Geyser]]. In addition to the Crypts, scrap piles can be found buried in the ground here. These waterlogged veins can be located using a [[Wishbone]] after defeating [[Bonemass]], though it should be noted that they tend to be uncommon and are generally not viable for providing any significant quantities of iron. Additionally, mining is a noisy activity and will attract the local fauna. == Creatures == ==== Hostile ==== * {{Item link|Blob}} * {{Item link|Oozer}} * {{Item link|Draugr}} * {{Item link|Draugr Elite}} * {{Item link|Leech}} * {{Item link|Skeleton}} * {{Item link|Surtling}} * {{Item link|Abomination}} * {{Item link|Wraith}} (night only) * {{Item link|Writhan}} * {{Item link|Seeker}} (at night after [[The Queen]] is defeated) * {{Item link|Charred Warrior}} (at night after [[Fader]] is defeated) * {{Item link|Charred Marksman}} (at night after [[Fader]] is defeated) ==== Passive ==== * {{Item link|Giant Herring}} == Resources == * {{Item link|Ancient Bark}} * {{Item link|Scrap Iron}} * {{Item link|Guck}} * {{Item link|Thistle}} * {{Item link|Turnip Seeds}} * {{Item link|Wood}} * {{Item link|Stone}} * {{Item link|Mushroom}} * Chests: (2-3 of the following) {{loot table| {{loot row|item=Amber |amt=1-5 |rate=11.8%}} {{loot row|item=Amber pearl |amt=1-3 |rate=11.8%}} {{loot row|item=Ancient bark |amt=20-30 |rate=11.8%}} {{loot row|item=Chain |amt=1 |rate=11.8%}} {{loot row|item=Coins |amt=20-60 |rate=11.8%}} {{loot row|item=Ironhead arrow |amt=10-15 |rate=11.8%}} {{loot row|item=Poison arrow |amt=10-15 |rate=11.8%}} {{loot row|item=Ruby |amt=1-3 |rate=11.8%}} {{loot row|item=Withered bone |amt=1 |rate=5.9%}} }} ==Alternative biomes== In addition to the regular [[Biomes]] generation, each local patch of biome has a chance to get an [[Alternative biomes]]. Once a Swamp is located, it is recommended that an adjacent [[Meadows]] or [[Black Forest]] is chosen for landfall. This way, it is significantly easier for a forward base to be erected and operated from. * There are various ways to glitch (i.e. through unintended ways) into a swamp crypt without using a key. These methods may be patched in later versions of the game. ** A popular strategy is to place a [[Chairs|chair]] just in front of the crypt entrance, sit in the chair, and then stand up. The player will be pushed through the gate and by extension, the loading barrier. ** The method listed above can also be utilized if a crypt is found to have an indestructible ancient tree blocking the entrance. == Gallery == Swamp1.jpg Swamp2.jpg Swamp Spawner.jpg Crypt 1.jpg Gravenimage.jpg|One of the statues found in the Swamp. {{infobox biome | title = Meadows | image = Biome meadows.png | caption = | passive = *[[Deer]] *[[Gull]] *[[Perch]] *[[Pike]] | hostile = *[[Boar]] *[[Greyling]] *[[Neck]] | boss = * [[Eikthyr]] | unique = | regular = * [[Beech]] * [[Birch]] * [[Oak]] * [[Flint]] * [[Stone]] * [[Dandelion]] | food = * [[Mushroom]] * [[Raspberry]] | structures = * [[Abandoned House]] * [[Abandoned Farm]] * [[Draugr Village]] * [[Dolmen]] * [[Ancient Stone Circle]] * [[Viking Graveyard]] * [[Sacrificial Stones]] * [[Combat Ruin]] | dungeons = | npcs = * [[Hildir]] * [[Blåbär]] * [[Hallon]] }} The '''Meadows''' are calm, innocuous [[biomes]] covered in grass and gentle rolling hills. They are the very first biome the player encounters in ''Valheim,'' making them simultaneously the least difficult. Large clearings and sloping hillsides are punctuated by thickets and forests of [[Beech]], [[Birch]], and [[Oak]] trees; underfoot is a carpet of ferns, saplings, and the occasional cluster of [[Raspberries|berry bushes]]. [[Deer]] and wild [[Boar|Boars]] graze peacefully from the grass while diminutive [[Greyling|Greylings]] scurry about, looking for structures and players to damage. Streams and rivers wind and carve their way through the landscape, sometimes opening up to inland seas and lakes, stout [[Neck|Necks]] bathing in the sun along their shores. On the whole, the Meadows make for some of the most pleasant vistas the tenth world has to offer. The biome is not without its hazards, however. Among the trees and numerous [[Abandoned Farm|structures]] left behind by their predecessors, the player can find various [[point of interest|points of interest]] while exploring, such as [[Viking Graveyard]]s and particularly deadly [[Draugr Village]]s. == Creatures == === Hostile === {| class="wikitable sortable mw-collapsible" style="text-align:center;" ! !style="text-align:center;"|Name !style="text-align:center;"|Primary Spawn !style="text-align:center;"|HP !style="text-align:center;"|Damageat 0 armor !class="unsortable" style="text-align:center;"|Notes |- |[[File:Boar.png|50x50px]] |[[Boar]] |[[Meadows]] |10 |7.5-10 | |- |[[File:Neck 0star.png|50x50px]] |[[Neck]] |[[Meadows]] |5 |5~ | |- |[[File:Greyling 0S.png|50x50px]] |[[Greyling]] |[[Meadows]] |20 |3-5 | |- |[[File:Draugr 0S.png|50x50px]] |[[Draugr]] |[[Swamp]] [[Meadows]] |100 |40-50 |In the Meadows, spawns in [[Draugr Village]]s, and anywhere on foggy nights after [[The Elder]] is defeated. {{infobox biome | title = Black Forest | image = Biome blackforest.png | caption = | passive = * [[Crow]] * [[Deer]] * [[Gull]] * [[Perch]] * [[Pike]] * [[Trollfish]] | hostile = * [[Bear]] * [[Ghost]] * [[Greydwarf]] * [[Greydwarf Brute]] * [[Greydwarf Shaman]] * [[Rancid Remains]] * [[Skeleton]] * [[Troll]] | boss = * [[Brenna]] (miniboss) * [[The Elder]] | unique = * [[Copper Ore]] from a [[Copper Deposit]] * [[Tin Ore]] from a [[Tin Deposit]] * [[Thistle]] * [[Carrot Seed]] | regular = | food = * [[Yellow Mushroom]] * [[Blueberries]] | structures = * [[Dolmen]] * [[Abandoned Outpost]] * [[Big Rock Clearing]] * [[Greydwarf Nest]] * [[Shipwreck]] | dungeons = * [[Troll Cave]] * [[Burial Chambers]] * [[Smouldering Tomb]] * [[Bear Cave]] | npcs = * [[Haldor]] * [[Halstein]] }} '''Black Forest''' [[biomes]] are dangerous, coniferous forests full of dense and lush vegetation. A low blanket of ferns, felled logs, stumps, [[Blueberries|berry bushes]], and [[Thistle]] plants is towered over by a canopy of [[Pine]] and [[Fir]] trees. Rolling hills and spacious dales are broken up by huge exposed boulders and slumbering [[Copper Deposit]]s. The coastline features many coves, inlets, and even marshlands. The shore is lined with glistening [[Tin Deposit]]s, ready to be collected. It is the only biome where [[Copper Ore|Copper]] and [[Tin Ore|Tin]] ores can be mined, available to the player after defeating [[Eikthyr]] and acquiring an [[Antler Pickaxe]]. Large amounts of [[Greydwarf]]s amble about this sea of trees, along with the occasional [[Troll]] and gaggle of [[Skeleton]]s. The forest is also home to [[Burial Chambers]], the first instanced dungeon area in the game. These chambers are the player's first source of [[Surtling Core]]s, which allow the creation of a [[Smelter|smelting yard]] and usher in the beginnings of metallurgy. Typically, the player will explore the Black Forest as their second biome, after the [[Meadows]]. == Creatures == ==== Hostile ==== * {{Item link|Bear}} * {{Item link|Greydwarf}} * {{Item {{infobox biome | title = Plains | image = Biome heath.png | caption = | passive = * [[Gull]] * [[Grouper]] | hostile = * [[Deathsquito]] * [[Fuling]] * [[Fuling Berserker]] * [[Fuling Shaman]] * [[Growth]] * [[Lox]] * [[Vile]] | boss = * [[Zil & Thungr]] (minibosses) * [[Yagluth]] | unique = * [[Flax]] * [[Barley]] * [[Tar]] | regular = [[Birch]] | food = [[Cloudberries]] | structures = * [[Fuling Village]] * [[Fuling Outpost]] * [[Fuling Ruin]] * [[Stonehenge]] * [[Tar Pit]] * [[Shipwreck]] | dungeons = [[Sealed Tower]] | npcs = }} The '''Plains''' are a wide open [[Biomes|biome]] with rolling hills and sparse trees. They are home to many different kinds of rock formations, some appearing to be natural (such as enormous destructible stone monoliths), and some constructed by the native [[Fuling]]s. Populated [[Fuling Village]]s can be seen spread across the Plains, built from [[Deer Hide]] and [[Bone Fragments]]. Despite their initially tranquil appearance, the Plains biome is difficult and dangerous to navigate. Resources uniquely found in the Plains enable the player to make weapons out of [[Black Metal]] and [[Linen Thread]], and food out of [[Barley Flour]] and [[Lox Meat]]. Finally, the Plains contain [[Tar]] in and around [[Tar Pit]]s, which allows the player to construct high-tier furniture and darkwood buildings or decorations. Be careful when sailing near the Plains as [[Deathsquito]]es can spawn on the beach and aggro far into the water. == Resources == * [[Birch]] * [[Cloudberries]] * [[Flax]] * [[Barley]] * [[Tar]] * Chests: (2-3 of the following) {{loot table| {{loot row|item=Barley |amt=2-4 |rate=13.9%}} {{loot row|item=Black metal scrap |amt=2-5 |rate=27.8%}} {{loot row|item=Coins |amt=10-40 |rate=27.8%}} {{loot row|item=Needle |amt=2-5 |rate=27.8%}} {{loot row|item=Sharpening stone |amt=1 |rate=2.8%}} }} == Creatures == * {{Item link|Deathsquito}} * {{Item link|Fuling}} * {{Item link|Fuling Berserker}} * {{Item link|Fuling Shaman}} * {{Item link|Growth}} * {{Item link|Lox}} * {{Item link|Vile}} (night only) * {{Item link|Skeleton}} (at night after [[Bonemass]] is defeated) * {{Item link|Draugr}} (on foggy nights after [[The Elder]] is defeated) * {{Item link|Seeker}} (at night after [[The Queen]] is defeated) * {{Item link|Charred Warrior}} (at night after [[Fader]] is defeated) * {{Item link|Charred Marksman}} (at night after [[Fader]] is defeated) ==== Passive ==== * {{Item link|Gull}} * {{Item link|Grouper}} ==Alternative biomes== In addition to the regular [[Biomes]] generation, each local patch of biome has a chance to get an [[Alternative biomes]]. {|class='wikitable' !Name !Changes !Number per world !Min Distance center !Exclude |- |Bones | Add [[Rancid Remains]] common spawn

{{infobox biome | title = Mountain | image = Biome mountain.png | caption = | passive = * [[Tetra]] | hostile = *[[Wolf]] *[[Drake]] *[[Stone Golem]] (Mountain / Frost Caves) *[[Fenring]] (At nighttime) *[[Draugr]] (Mountain towers) *[[Skeleton]] (Mountain towers / Cabins) *[[Bat]] (Frost Caves) *[[Ulv]] (Frost Caves) *[[Cultist]] (Frost Caves) | boss = * [[Geirrhafa]] (miniboss) * [[Moder]] | unique = * [[Obsidian]] * [[Dragon Egg]] * [[Silver Ore]] from [[Silver Vein]] * [[Onion Seeds]] | regular = | food = | structures = * [[Mountain Tower]] * [[Abandoned Cabin]] * [[Inverted Tower]] * [[Mountain grave]] * [[Drake Nest]] * [[Cairns]] * [[Forge of Potential]] | dungeons = * [[Frost Caves]] * [[Howling Cavern]] | npcs = }} The '''Mountain''' is a [[Biomes|biome]] which features frozen snow covered peaks framed with [[Fir]] trees. This frozen and unforgiving region is home to [[Wolf|Wolves]] and others [[Fenring|sons]] of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fenrir Fenrir]. [[Drake]]s, the offspring of [[Moder]], can be found in the skies making their nests at its peaks where they lay their [[Dragon Egg]]s. Beware shifting piles of stone, they might be more alive than you think, stirring the resting [[Stone Golem]]. Mountains can also contain [[Frost Caves]], which are a dungeon home to [[Cultist]]s and their pet [[Ulv]]. [[Bat]]s also make their home here and can startle unsuspecting Vikings. [[Crystal]]s can be found growing naturally on the walls and occasionally contain a large underground lake, be careful not to wake the [[Stone Golem]] that can also be resting there. Going into the mountain biome will cause the [[Freezing]] effect on the player. This effect can be negated by drinking [[Frost Resistance Mead]], wearing a [[Lox Cape]], a [[Wolf Fur Cape]], a [[Fenris Coat]], a [[Feather Cape]], or wearing the [[Wolf armor chest]]. The [[Wolf armor legs]] do not offer frost resistance. This effect is also negated by nearby campfires. == Resources == * [[Silver]] - Veins of [[Silver Ore]] can be located buried beneath the snow of the mountains. These veins can be located using a [[Wishbone]], which is acquired by defeating [[Bonemass]]. Silver veins require an [[Iron Pickaxe]] or better to mine. * [[Obsidian]] - Obsidian nodes spawn in above ground on the mountain, which can be used to make [[Obsidian Arrow]]s. They require an [[Iron Pickaxe]] or better to mine. * [[Onion Seeds]] - Located in chests, usually in abandoned shacks. * [[Dragon Egg]] - One lies in the center of every [[Drake Nest]]. * Chests: (2-4 of the following) {{loot table| {{loot row|item=Amber |amt=1-6 |rate=14.3%}} {{loot row|item=Amber pearl |amt=2-5 |rate=14.3%}} {{loot row|item=Coins |amt=16-41 |rate=14.3%}} {{loot row|item=Coins |amt=30-55 |rate=14.3%}} {{loot row|item=Frost arrow |amt=5-10 |rate=14.3%}} {{loot row|item=Ruby |amt=1-2 |rate=14.3%}} {{loot row|item=Obsidian |amt=5-10 |rate=14.3%}} }} == Creatures == === Hostile === * {{Item link|Moder}} * {{Item link|Wolf}} * {{Item link|Drake}}s * {{Item link|Stone Golem}}s * {{Item link|Fenring}}s (At nighttime) * {{Item link|Draugr}} (Mountain towers) * {{Item link|Skeleton}}s (Mountain towers / Cabins; anywhere at night after [[Bonemass]] is defeated) * {{Item link|Bat}} (Inside [[Frost Caves]]) * {{Item link|Ulv}} (Inside [[Frost Caves]]) * {{Item link|Cultist}} (Inside [[Frost Caves]]) * {{Item link|Fuling}}s (At nighttime, after [[Yagluth]] is defeated) * {{Item link|Seeker}}s (At nighttime, after [[The Queen]] is defeated) * {{Item link|Charred Warrior}}s (At nighttime, after [[Fader]] is defeated) * {{Item link|Charred Marksman|Charred Marksmen}} (At nighttime, after [[Fader]] is defeated) ==== Passive ==== * {{Item link|Tetra}} (Inside [[Frost Caves]]) ==Alternative biomes== In addition to the regular [[Biomes]] generation, each local patch of biome has a chance to get an [[Alternative biomes]]. The '''Deep North''' is a vast, snowy [[Biomes|biome]], found in the northernmost part of ''Valheim''. Described as a "postcard of a Christmas landscape", it contrasts the hordes of the fiery [[Ashlands]] with fewer but stronger creatures.

Akin to the Ashlands, the Deep North landmass is separated from other biomes by an [[Ocean]] and borders the [[World Edge]] on the northern side. There is no equivalent of the boiling sea preventing access to the biome, however, defeating [[Fader]] is still required to progress through the biome, and strong enemies pose a threat. Sheets of ice float along the shores, a potential danger to any ship attempting to dock here.

As in the Mountains, all weather in the Deep North is freezing, day and night, so players without frost resistant clothes or [[Frost Resistance Mead]] in effect take continuous [[Freezing Effect|freezing]] damage outdoors. See [[#Weather|Weather]] below.

The biome was the focus of the [[Version history|1.0 update]].

The forests consist mostly of [[Timber Tree]]s, along with smaller snowy firs, old stumps and fallen logs, all of which yield {{Item link|Timberwood}}. Snowy branches lying on the ground can be picked up for Timberwood, and snowballs can be picked up as well. Lingonberry bushes are scattered across the biome, and wild Kale occasionally grows, giving three {{Item link|Kale Seeds}} when picked.

Sheets of floating ice cover the water near the shore and can be broken for three to five {{Item link|Ice}}. Frozen statues of Greydwarfs and Skeletons can also be broken for Ice and {{Item link|Resin}}.

Wind intensity is capped at 1. A blizzard's wind range lies above that cap, so the wind always blows at full strength during a blizzard.

A player outdoors and away from a fire gets the [[Freezing Effect|Freezing]] effect: no health regeneration, 60% slower stamina and eitr regeneration, and one point of damage every second. Near a fire or in shelter, the player gets the [[Cold Effect|Cold]] effect instead (50% slower health regeneration, 25% slower stamina and eitr regeneration), and a fire in shelter removes both. Slight, normal or very high frost resistance prevents both effects.

While it snows, snow builds up on structures that have no roof above them and are not inside a [[Shield Generator]]'s shield. It can be cleared with the [[Snow Shovel]].

It is full of valleys, dales, ravines, and even plateaus punctuated by gargantuan black crags that often peek over the mist. [[Yggdrasil Shoot]]s grow on these rocks. Larger, glowing [[Ancient Roots|Yggdrasil roots]] can be found lining the ground, often visible through the mist. Its coastline is equally treacherous, greeting the longship with sheer cliffs, steep wharfs, and rocky sandbars. [[Wisplight]]s and placeable [[Wisp Torch]]es can be used to clear out the permeating mist, but both require [[Yagluth]] to be defeated. This biome is oppressive, being quite difficult to navigate, often to the point of disorientation. The enemies are tough and will most often see the player before the player sees them. [[Seeker]]s and [[Seeker Soldier]]s are the most common enemies, able to chase the player nearly constantly. Standard Seekers even have the ability to fly if they need to access higher areas of the slopes. Also residing here is a player-neutral race of [[Dvergr (race)|Dvergr]], who will actively fight enemies to defend their keeps. Should the player attack them as well, they will prove to be formidable foes. The Mistlands, alongside [[Version history|its content update]], introduces a new combat mechanic called [[Eitr]]. It is acquired by eating specific foods made from the biome's crops and creatures, such as [[Magecap]]s. The '''Ocean''' is a [[Biomes|biome]] made up of, much like examples in real life, a vast body of water. It is only realistically accessible by [[boats]], as swimming out from the safety of the shore quickly depletes [[stamina]] and leads to drowning. In many ways, the Ocean acts as less its own dedicated biome, per se, and more a vehicle for player exploration.

Currently the biome only features the elusive and destructive [[Serpent]] enemy as well as the even more elusive [[Leviathan]], a hulking shelled creature covered in shrubbery, algae, and barnacles. These two creatures are the sole way for players to gather [[Serpent Scale|Serpent scales]] and [[Chitin]], respectively.
